text:
Anton Lundell has gone from a target of criticism to one of Florida's hottest forwards inside a week. Last Word On Sports wrote on Nov. 17 that his bottom-six play was underwhelming; four days later The Hockey Writers called him key to the Panthers' season. Both had a point.

He has 6 goals in his last ten games, ahead of the chances (3.5 expected) that produced them, so the goal streak is partly hot hands. But the bigger picture runs the other way. With Lundell on the ice at 5-on-5, Florida takes 56% of the expected goals and has scored 5.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve. That has kept his assist total at 4 when his play says it should be higher, and gaps like that usually swing back.

The two-time Stanley Cup winner draws tough minutes, 90th percentile competition by Evolving-Hockey's count last season. Points may lag, but the process is the reason he keeps getting the matchups.
